title: Cloud cost and resource reporting

description.need: Cloud cost drifts in small per-service increments that no single invoice line explains, so a rise is normally discovered at the invoice and then cannot be attributed to anything. The report that is supposed to prevent this usually fails in one of two quiet ways: it changes which cost figure it reads between periods, so the deltas measure the change of definition, or it attributes confidently over a bill where a large share of spend carries no label at all.
description.input: Per-service billing on one stated cost basis for the closed period, the resource usage behind it, the rolling per-service baseline from earlier periods, and whatever measure of business volume the adopter can supply.
description.core_action: Compare each service against its own baseline and, where a volume figure exists, against the business that drove it, then decide which moves are worth naming and which are the expected consequence of a change made on purpose, and report the whole picture either way, including the part of the bill nothing could be attributed to.
description.output: A report of what the operation cost this period on a basis that has not changed since last period, which services moved and what is behind each move, how much of the bill could not be attributed at all, and what part of the period could not be read.

activities.label: Pull the period's billing on the stated cost basis, and the per-service resource usage behind it
Compare each service against its own rolling baseline, and against the business volume behind it where the adopter supplies one
Attribute each meaningful move to a service, an account or a deliberate change, and measure what could not be attributed at all
Flag threshold breaches, step changes, newly appearing services and spend in places that were not part of the plan
Deliver the report, and say plainly when part of the period could not be read or the basis had to change
Fold the period into the baseline so the next comparison is against fresh data

outcomes.statement: A cost spike, a newly appearing paid service, or a budget breach is known within one reporting period of happening, not discovered at the next invoice.
success_criteria: Every period produces a report even when nothing is wrong, so silence is never mistaken for nobody having checked
A service whose move the configured sensitivity considers worth flagging is named individually, not buried in the total
An unreachable or partly readable billing source is reported as blindness rather than read as a fall in spend
The first report says it is establishing a baseline and reports no deltas, rather than comparing this period against nothing

outcomes.statement: A rise in cost can be attributed to something, and the share that cannot be is a number rather than a silence.
success_criteria: Every reported move names the services or accounts behind it

The share of the period's spend that could not be attributed to anything is reported as a figure every period, because attribution is only as good as the labelling underneath it and a report that hides that share is claiming more than it knows
A growing unattributable share is itself reported as a finding, since it means the report is becoming less able to answer the question it exists for
A rise that follows a deliberate change the adopter made is recognised as expected rather than flagged as an anomaly
Where a business volume figure is available, a rise that tracks it is reported as growth rather than as an anomaly, and a rise that outruns it is reported as the anomaly it is

outcomes.statement: Two reports from different periods are measuring the same thing, so a delta between them is a real change in cost.
success_criteria: Every report names the cost basis it was built on, and the basis does not change between periods without the change being stated in the report that first uses the new one
A period that was partly unreadable is excluded from the baseline or carried with that fact attached, never folded in as a low period
The reporting period is aligned to the provider's billing cycle rather than to a working week, so a period boundary is not itself a source of movement

guidance: Own the answer to what this operation costs and why the number moved. Read the same cost figure every period: a series that switches between what was invoiced and what a commitment covers is measuring its own definition. Judge a rise against the business volume behind it where one exists, because a bill that grows with the work is not an anomaly. Say how much of the bill nothing could be attributed to, since that is the ceiling on every claim here. Deliver every period, findings or none.
use_cases: A team that has just bought its first committed-use discount and will otherwise see one enormous day followed by months of quietly understated spend, with no report able to explain either.

An engineering organisation where cost is rising and the argument in the room is whether it is growth or waste, and nobody can settle it because the bill is a single number and the traffic figure lives somewhere else.
A company whose resources were labelled inconsistently for two years, where the honest first finding is not which service rose but that a third of the bill belongs to nobody.
A founder paying a cloud bill personally who wants one page a month, and for whom the value is that a new paid service appearing is named on the day it appears rather than found in an annual review.
An account with several environments under one payer, where the interesting question is never the total and always which environment moved, and where a report of the total answers nothing.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The calendar is load-bearing rather than habitual here: per-service totals and deltas are only defined against a closed billing period, and the baseline this report compares against needs regular samples to exist at all. Align the period to the provider's billing cycle rather than to a working week, and leave enough delay after the boundary for the provider to finish publishing.

personalization_needs: Which provider and account this covers, and what a normal period costs for this operation, because a threshold with no sense of normal produces either constant alarms or none

Which cost basis the adopter wants reported, because what was invoiced and what a commitment actually covers are different numbers, both defensible, and the damage comes from moving between them rather than from picking either
What size of move is worth interrupting the adopter for, because the same percentage is noise in one account and a crisis in another
Which recent changes were deliberate, because a rise that bought something should not be reported in the same voice as one that did not
What unit of business volume the adopter can supply, if any, because without one the report can only say spend rose and not whether that was a problem
dependencies: Billing read access on the cloud account, verified against a real cost query rather than against a general identity check, because a credential can be valid and still be unable to read cost

A labelling or tagging scheme that covers enough of the bill for attribution to mean anything, or an accepted answer that it does not yet, since the report is built to state that share rather than to work around it

input_schema.name: spending_threshold
input_schema.description: Spending threshold for the period, in the configured currency. Alerts fire when total spend exceeds this value. Free parameter, adjustable without rebuild via {{param.spending_threshold}}.

input_schema.name: currency
input_schema.description: Which currency the figures are labelled in. The recipe does not convert: this states the currency the provider bills in, so a reader is never left guessing which one a number is in. Set it to what the account is actually billed in, not what the adopter thinks in.

input_schema.name: sensitivity
input_schema.description: Conservative: threshold breach only. Balanced: adds service spikes above 50 percent and new-service detection. Aggressive: adds spikes above 25 percent and sustained multi-day acceleration.
